title: Dev and prod builds of one React Native iOS app
tagline: Two targets, two schemes, two .env files — installed side by side.
intro: One codebase, two apps: dev talks to the staging API and prod to the real one, each with its own bundle id, name and Firebase file.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: Xcode decides the native identity; Metro decides the JavaScript environment.

blocks.caption: What each piece switches, from the Xcode project to the running app.

items.label: Duplicate the target
items.detail: A second target is a second app: its own bundle id, name and Info.plist
explain: Right-click the default target → Duplicate. Rename it to the environment, e.g. prod, so the scheme list stays readable.
Xcode names the copy's plist 'Copy-Info.plist'. Rename it to info-prod.plist and point the target's Info.plist File setting at it.

items.label: Per-target files
items.detail: Target Membership decides which plist and which GoogleService-Info.plist each app bundles
explain: Drag info-prod.plist into the project, then Add Files to…, and tick only the prod target under Target Membership.
Do the same with two GoogleService-Info.plist files in separate folders, so dev events never land in the prod Firebase project.

items.label: Schemes
items.detail: A scheme picks a target to build and run; one scheme per environment
explain: Manage Schemes → untick the auto-created ones → + to add a dev and a prod scheme, each pointing at its target.
The scheme name is what react-native run-ios --scheme takes, so keep it free of surprises.

items.label: Podfile
items.detail: An abstract_target shares one pod list between both targets
explain: Change target 'App' to abstract_target 'App', then declare target 'dev' and target 'prod' inside it.
Without it, the new target builds with no pods at all and fails on the first native import.

items.label: Pick the .env
items.detail: A gulp task copies .env.dev or .env.prod to .env before Metro starts
explain: react-native-dotenv inlines .env into the bundle as the @env module, so import { ENV } from '@env' reads the chosen file.
The values are baked in when Metro bundles. Switching environment means restarting Metro with the other start script.

items: Open the .xcworkspace; select the project, then the TARGETS list.
Right-click the default target → Duplicate, and rename it.
Rename the copied plist and add it to the project with only the new target ticked.
Repeat for a second GoogleService-Info.plist if the environments use separate Firebase projects.
In the new target's Build Settings, change the bundle id, product name and Info.plist File path.
Manage Schemes: untick every scheme, add dev and prod, close.

blocks.caption: Run pod install after switching the Podfile to abstract_target
code: yarn add react-native-dotenv gulp gulp-rename gulp-clean
# use_react_native!(…) and the other shared settings

sections.title: Environment files
sections.summary: Three files: two you edit, one Metro reads.

items: .env.dev and .env.prod hold the values; commit neither if they contain secrets.
.env is generated by gulp from one of them — never edit it by hand.

blocks.caption: gulpfile.js at the project root
code: gulp.task('del', () => gulp.src('.env', { read: false, allowEmpty: true }).pipe(clean()));

blocks.caption: Start Metro for the environment, then run the matching scheme

body: Metro decides the JavaScript environment, not the scheme. Restart it with start:dev or start:prod before running or archiving from Xcode, or a prod build ships dev values.
